title: Miles Regis
deck: An artist's paintings, redrawn by hand for a coloring book.
lede: Miles Regis paints crowds of figures and words. For his coloring book, each painting was redrawn by hand as a black line, leaving the color to the reader.
challenge: The artist Miles Regis was making a coloring book from his paintings, and they needed to become black-and-white illustrations without losing what made them his.
work: Each drawing keeps the artist's composition and his words, figure for figure, and turns the paint into an open line that leaves the color to whoever holds the pencil.
A painting of figures under the words “Respect my pronouns” becomes a clean line drawing of the same scene, and a crowd in printed tees becomes “Does my shirt have that much power?” in line.
deliverables: Black-and-white line illustrations, adapted from the paintings
